finding.observed: The canonical /readyz implementation checked UnifiedDB schema/users/sessions/generation only. Service startup creates both managed tmux/Claude sessions, but readiness did not re-check their continued existence.
finding.risk: After a managed Claude/tmux session exits, the container can continue returning HTTP 200 ready while the advertised permanent-Claude-terminal product surface is partially or fully dead.
finding.counterhypothesis: Boot-time TerminalSessionManager.ensure() makes a separate live-terminal readiness probe unnecessary.
finding.counterhypothesis_result: REJECTED: boot-time existence is not a durable liveness guarantee; managed tmux policy does not set remain-on-exit, so direct Claude process exit can remove the session while UnifiedDB remains healthy.

repair.readiness_contract: UnifiedDB state ready AND gabriel managed tmux session live AND andreas managed tmux session live

execution.scope: reconstructed relevant readiness helper/source slice plus exact test semantics

vercel.reason: Fresh Vercel Git-preview execution remains admission-blocked before build/Sandbox start by the observed account deployment rate limit; repeating it would not discriminate this readiness mechanism.

next_gate: In the next actually-started authorized exact-current container run: prove /readyz=200 with both managed Claude/tmux sessions alive, terminate exactly one managed Claude process, prove /readyz becomes 503 without mutating UnifiedDB, then restore through the admitted product lifecycle and prove readiness returns only after both sessions are live.
